analysis: Only scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py changed, and it is a CI test harness, not provider runtime code. Changes: run_labels() helper, LINUX/MACOS now carry a run-scoped profile label (e.g. darkbloom-macos-arm64-run-<RUN_ID>), sized() produces run-scoped sized labels, and two new tests. Those tests check that the route request carries the X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1 header with an unchanged body key set, and that the router accepts only exact current-run label arrays and rejects legacy, other-run and extra-label grants (lines ~422-471). Existing assertions on fallback, forks never contacting the plane, certificate verification, HTTPS-only, and workflow-command and markdown injection were retained. The tests tighten the CI-runner routing control, so a runner registered for an older run cannot be selected by a later run. I saw no weakening of assertions, no new attack surface, and no secrets. The test workflow files, the router script (darkbloom-route.yml) and the plane's behaviour are outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the router implements what the tests assert. The test changes touch none of the threat-model assets (A-001..A-020) or trust boundaries (TB-002..TB-014), including the provider runtime and T-041. They do not regress any of them. A further review pass needs the darkbloom-route.yml diff to confirm the header and label logic match the tests; this is an integration question, not a finding.
